Author: @oricatttt
Content: honest opinion - really disappointed in this recipe :/ I've had this video saved in a playlist for several weeks and was so excited to make it, and it completely failed. Having baked a good amount I felt a little skeptical about some of the steps/corners being cut, but tried to follow the recipe anyway. Ultimately though all those things proved there's a reason why the baking world does things a certain way. 1. the chocolate seized and became grainy and separated (you can see in the video as well), from using the mixer with the egg whites still on them. This happened for my batter as well, which makes for a bit of a buttery mess. 2. powdered sugar is drastically different from brown sugar, and I found the meringue much sweeter and more icing like in flavor. 3. 1 tsp of espresso powder is a *lot* for the amount of batter and, indeed, the coffee flavor comes through strongly in the cookie, which I'm not a fan of. 4. tradition says to fold for a reason. I'm not sure if it's from the beating or if it's from the chocolate having seized earlier (resulting in a split of fat & everything else), but when introducing the egg white and chocolate mixture together, the batter completely collapsed and became much thinner than the video. The result was all the cookies spread into one large pan cookie, and very flat instead of light and fluffy, with no crackles on top. I mean I'm still gonna eat it, but they definitely did not come out like the video, which I'm sad about

Author: @lucaslepesteur7846
Content:
Just to point out you don't need a double boiler for swiss meringue, you can set your burner the lowest and just mix until the sugar is dissolved. Just keep scraping the bottom of the pan with the spatula so the egg whites don't curdle.

Same with chocolate, just mix it scraping the bottom to not let it burn.

I always do this way for my lemon pies because swiss meringue can be frozen and stay put for a few days, while french meringue like what is done in the video will deflate and get watery sooner thats why you bake them in the oven.

Author: @TocsTheWanderer
Content:
There's a gluten-free peanut butter cookie recipe I've recently done that I really like.
1 cup creamy peanut butter
1/2 cup sugar (can add more if you want)
1 large egg
Mix the ingredients, no need to whip the sugar with the peanut butter, just mix it all until combined. Form balls and press down onto baking sheet with a fork, should make 12 small-ish cookies. Bake at 350°F for 10 minutes.
They're not super sweet, but with no flour to get in the way, they taste super peanut-y. They're also kinda crumbly, but again, not really a big deal in my book.
